Warning.description: Something the operation did differently from what was asked, in the plugin's words.

id.description: The operation's ID, set by whoever applies the plan: the same for every attempt at one request.

basis.description: What the plan was computed from, when the snapshot gives versions: every file it writes, every path it creates (as must not exist), and every file whose content decided the outcome (the Matter an Action is filed under).

settingsVersion.description: The settings' version the plan was computed with (statuses, types and Spheres decide what it writes).

Plan.description:
The writes an operation needs. Apply creates, then edits, then bodies, then renames: paths in edits and bodies are the paths before any rename. Edits name `mtm-` keys only; every other key and line stays as it is.

A plan is applied only if what it was computed from still holds: every `basis` entry at its version (or still absent), and the settings at `settingsVersion`. Otherwise nothing is written and the operation is planned again.

FrontmatterEntry.description: A frontmatter entry of a new note; entries are written in this order.

BodyEdit.description: A change to a note's body, applied with `applyBodyEdit`; only the lines it targets change.

BasisEntry.description: A file a plan was computed from: its version when read, or null when it must not exist.

Change.description: What a write changes, one entry per property, body part or file; values are null when absent.

files.description: In the order they were first touched: new notes, then edited notes, then notes whose links a rename rewrote.

links.description: Notes whose links a rename rewrote ("Automatically update internal links" on).

danglingLinks.description: How many links point nowhere after the plan (renames with that setting off).

linkChanges.description: Each link a rename rewrote or left pointing nowhere, paths as before the rename.

FileOutcome.description: Everything a plan does to the files.

from.description: Where it is now: the same path, the old path of a renamed note, or null for a new file.

before.description: Its content when the plan was applied (null for a new file); a writer refuses to write if the file differs by then.

changes.description: The lines that differ between `before` and `after`.

line.description: 1-based, in the file after the write; for a removed line, the line that now stands where it was.

LineChange.description: One changed line: replaced (both texts), added (`before` null) or removed (`after` null).

LinkUpdate.description: Links a rename rewrote in one note: the note's path after the plan and the lines (1-based).

path.description: The note holding the link, as it is named before the rename.

key.description: The property holding the link (`see.1`), for links in properties.

after.description: Null for a link left pointing nowhere.

LinkChange.description: A link a rename touched or left behind.

frontmatter.description: The properties; null when the note has none the core can read.

end.description: Where the properties block ends: its closing line and the offset after it; null with no properties.

bodyLine.description: The first line of the body.

op.description: The request's operation, when it could be read.

field.description: Where it went wrong. For the operations' own errors, the input field by its public name, as other tools name it (`waiting-on`, `due-from`); for the boundary's, a JSON Pointer into the request (`/input/title`, `/snapshot/now`).

candidates.description: For `ambiguous`: what matched. For `unmatched`: the valid labels.

writeCode.description: For `write-failed`: why the files layer refused the plan, and the file.

CoreErrorCode.description: Why a request failed. The operations' own codes (`not-found`, `ambiguous`, `unmatched`, `invalid`, `not-ready`) and the boundary's: a request that isn't valid JSON or doesn't fit the schema (`bad-request`), a boundary version the core doesn't speak (`unsupported-boundary`), a snapshot that contradicts itself (`bad-snapshot`), too few IDs (`not-enough-ids`), a plan that can't be applied to the snapshot's files (`write-failed`), and anything unexpected (`internal`, a bug), and a held snapshot the core doesn't hold (`unknown-snapshot`: closed, or the core loaded again).
